dimension.category_description: How interaction crosses sensory, physical, spatial, embodied, or representational channels.
dimension.classification_boundary: The channel, embodiment, or rendering must be the load-bearing interface mechanism.

candidates.title: I Felt Bad After We Ignored Her: Understanding How Interface-Driven Social Prominence Shapes Group Discussions with GenAI
candidates.why: The agent occupies a human seat at the roundtable and speaks from that position, making its rendered body both the locus of its turns and the mechanism that grants it social prominence in group discussion.
candidates.over_the_runner_up: It edges out HAT Swapping because the evidence establishes both human-slot occupancy and embodied turn-taking, while the instructor stand-in quote establishes role substitution but not how outputs issue from the figure.
candidates.pattern_summary: The agent is given a rendered body — an animated character, a 3-D figure, an on-screen avatar, a participant tile — and the user addresses that figure rather than a text pane.
candidates.structural_signature: A persistent visual figure with its own extent and position is rendered in the interface, and the system's outputs are attributed to and emitted from that figure rather than from an undifferentiated output region. The figure occupies a slot ordinarily held by a human participant (a tile, a seat, a character in a scene).
candidates.pattern_curator_notes: I retained the first two consensus choices but selected consensus #4, rid 4423, instead of #3, rid 10283. Future You is conceptually distinctive and experimentally isolates embodiment, but its abstract-level evidence only names a photorealistic talking avatar; it does not clearly demonstrate the persistent positioned figure required by the structural signature. No score adjustment exceeds 0.3. Readers should still treat persistence and exact on-screen extent as partly inferred for rid 12692 and rid 4423: their quotes establish an embodied role and expressive output but do not describe the full layout. Rid 5135 has the strongest structural evidence, although its figure caption likewise provides limited rendering detail.

candidates.title: Sonic Stage: Automatically Generating an Interactive Spatial Soundscape to Facilitate Dialogue Video Comprehension for Blind and Low Vision Viewers
candidates.why: A particularly complete captured-video instance: 3D reconstruction locates and tracks characters, then positions each character’s dialogue at those scene-derived coordinates, making audio placement depend on the moving referent rather than a fixed channel or panel.
candidates.over_the_runner_up: It edges out SocialCue because the evidence explicitly connects reconstructed 3D character tracking to referent-bound output in captured video, while also avoiding a second, closely similar headset-based spatial-audio exemplar.
candidates.pattern_summary: Generated content is placed in the coordinate frame of a real scene, or of captured video of one, and attached to a referent within it rather than to a panel.
candidates.structural_signature: Rendering requires a spatial resolution step: the system extracts positions of referents in the scene and lays out output at those coordinates, so an output element's location is a function of scene geometry rather than of a layout slot. Losing tracking loses placement, not content.
candidates.pattern_curator_notes: I departed from the consensus order by selecting rid 9539 instead of third-ranked rid 9587. SocialCue is structurally strong, but it substantially overlaps Sonic Stage as another accessibility-oriented spatial-audio system; rid 9539 supplies clearer observable motion coupling and greater modality breadth without sacrificing structural fit. No score was adjusted by more than 0.3. Readers should distrust any implication of measured user benefit: the supplied evidence establishes rendering mechanisms, not outcomes. Guided Reality’s excerpt establishes spatial anchoring but does not explicitly confirm behavior when a referent moves, and Sonic Stage’s movement coupling is inferred from character tracking rather than stated verbatim.

candidates.title: Semantic See-through Goggles: Wearing Linguistic Virtual Reality in (Artificial) Intelligence
candidates.why: This is the canonical exemplar: live camera imagery crosses from image to text and back to generated image, with only the terminal reconstruction reaching the wearer and no direct-view bypass.
candidates.over_the_runner_up: It outranks WebPerceptor because its evidence explicitly establishes the complete capture-to-display chain, cross-representation losses, and displacement of the original signal.
candidates.pattern_summary: A chain of generative transformations is placed inside the user's perceptual path, so that what the user perceives is the pipeline's reconstruction rather than the captured signal.
candidates.structural_signature: Capture → transform₁ → … → transformₙ → display, wired in series with no bypass: the sensor's output never reaches the display directly, and the display shows only the terminal transform's output. The chain typically crosses representations (signal → symbolic → signal), and the loss at each crossing is what the user perceives. Transplants to audio (mic → transcript → resynthesis → earpiece), text streams, or any sensed-and-displayed channel. For the experiential reading the same wiring holds, with one additional negative residue: no explanatory or visualization element for the model property being conveyed appears anywhere in the interface.
candidates.pattern_curator_notes: I retained the consensus top three and their order. I reduced ShadAR from 3.58 to 3.2 because its LLM generates the shader upstream; the continuously interposed operation is shader-based rather than an explicit signal-to-symbolic-to-signal generative reconstruction. Readers should treat WebPerceptor's no-bypass property as strongly implied rather than directly stated, and ShadAR's exclusive displacement of unfiltered passthrough as implied by the rendering description. None of the supplied evidence reports user outcomes, so impact remains provisional. The lower-ranked candidates were not promoted despite their potentially interesting subject matter because their quotes fail to establish the defining continuous, unavoidable capture-to-transform-to-display structure.

candidates.over_the_runner_up: It outranks ShadAR because the LLM directly transforms the content users perceive in real time, whereas ShadAR's generative model creates a shader upstream and the live transformation is then conventional shader execution.

candidates.title: Dynamite: Real-Time Debriefing Slide Authoring through AI-Enhanced Multimodal Interaction
candidates.why: This is the clearest structural match: drawn circles or brush marks identify visual referents while simultaneous speech supplies the requested operation, and both channels are fused into one command. The concrete examples make the interaction directly reconstructable and transferable to other visual workspaces.
candidates.over_the_runner_up: Dynamite outranks One Kiss because its evidence demonstrates simultaneous channel fusion at the level of an individual command, rather than only describing complementary inputs to a generation request.
candidates.pattern_summary: Two or more physically distinct input channels — typed text, drawn marks, speech, pointing, body pose, GUI controls — are accepted for the same operation.
candidates.structural_signature: The input side of one operation has at least two capture channels feeding a single request object, and the system must fuse or arbitrate between them. The user can switch channels mid-operation without transitioning the interface to a different state, so channel choice is not a mode.
candidates.pattern_curator_notes: I retained consensus ranks 1 and 3 but promoted rank 4 GazePointAR over rank 2 SketchGPT. SketchGPT substantially overlaps Dynamite's sketch-plus-speech design, and its abstract-level evidence establishes integration less concretely; GazePointAR adds a distinct and structurally explicit example of multimodal arbitration. All score adjustments are below 0.3. Readers should treat claims about conflict handling, timing, and observed user benefit cautiously: One Kiss and GazePointAR are supported here only by abstracts, while even Dynamite's supplied excerpt demonstrates successful combinations but not how contradictory channels are resolved.

It is a strong example of multimodal input enabling orthogonal control dimensions that either channel alone could not express as effectively.
candidates.over_the_runner_up: One Kiss outranks GazePointAR because the evidence specifies exactly what information each channel contributes, making the fusion mechanism more reconstructable despite its narrower domain.

candidates.title: When Refreshable Tactile Displays Meet Conversational Agents: Investigating Accessible Data Presentation and Analysis with Touch and Speech
candidates.why: A 40-by-60 actuated pin array turns generated graphics into refreshable physical relief that users explore by touch, making material arrangement—not a rendered screen—the load-bearing output channel.
candidates.over_the_runner_up: It ranks above Generative Muscle Stimulation because its tangible output mechanism is equally explicit but supports a broader range of tasks with fewer safety and calibration constraints.
candidates.pattern_summary: At least one end of the interaction loop lives in matter rather than pixels: objects are grasped, moved, or posed to issue commands, or the system's output is delivered as physical motion, staged space, or a tangible arrangement.
candidates.structural_signature: Either the sensed event that constitutes a command is a physical manipulation of an object or body in space, or the emitted result is actuation or placement in space with no rendered layer required. The interface's layout is described in room coordinates, zones, and objects rather than in windows and widgets.
candidates.pattern_curator_notes: The selected set preserves the consensus top three but swaps the two tied 4.60 candidates: Shape n’ Swarm ranks second because it provides the most complete and broadly reusable tangible loop, while Generative Muscle Stimulation ranks third because specialized hardware, calibration, agency, and safety concerns constrain transfer. No score adjustment exceeds 0.3. Readers should distrust any implication of demonstrated outcome gains: the supplied evidence consists of isolated abstract, figure, or system-description excerpts. It establishes interface structure well, but does not consistently establish evaluation results, implementation robustness, user control, or real-world deployment.

candidates.title: Rambler: Supporting Writing With Speech via LLM-Assisted Gist Manipulation
candidates.why: Rambler makes speech the entry point for long-form composition, then converts spoken trains of thought into keywords, summaries, and conceptual units that support higher-level revision—an unusually complete and consequential instance of voice replacing typed authoring.
candidates.over_the_runner_up: Rambler ranks above VoiceAlign because it demonstrates a fuller end-to-end authoring experience and a more substantial redesign of work around speech, rather than adapting utterances for an existing voice interface.
candidates.pattern_summary: The user drives the system by speaking, and the spoken utterance occupies the slot that a typed prompt or a direct-manipulation action would otherwise occupy.
candidates.structural_signature: An audio-capture channel is the entry point of the control flow; the utterance is converted to an internal command, instruction sequence, or code, and that conversion product is what the rest of the system consumes. Nothing else in the flow requires the user to touch a pointer or keyboard, and the surface that would normally accept typed or pointed input is either absent or bypassed.
candidates.pattern_curator_notes: The final selection follows the consensus top three, but Orality is adjusted from 4.65 to 4.50 because its single figure-caption quote does not explain how speech is parsed, structured, or corrected. Rambler’s evidence clearly establishes speech-first capture and generated conceptual representations, although subsequent revisions may also use manual controls; this is permitted by the definition but makes it less structurally pure than VoiceAlign. VoiceAlign’s evidence is exceptionally direct, but its claimed impact rests only on the abstract-level mechanism rather than outcomes shown here. Orality’s evidence is the weakest of the three: readers should distrust any inference about the exact speech-to-graph conversion beyond the stated input-to-canvas relationship. NaviNote was the closest excluded candidate; its accessibility impact is strong, but the supplied quote shows voice-operated functions without the internal command or instruction representation consumed downstream.

candidates.title: Language of Zelda: Facilitating Language Learning Practices Using ChatGPT
candidates.why: Each NPC dialogue item is immediately rendered in its original form and as an adjacent English translation, cleanly instantiating the pattern’s same-content fan-out across language representations.
candidates.over_the_runner_up: Selected over rid 3456 because its immediately juxtaposed bilingual renderings demonstrate a broader representational form of multimodal output than conventional optional text-to-speech.
candidates.pattern_summary: One unit of system output is rendered in two or more sensory or representational channels at once — text plus speech, text plus image plus sound, or one language plus another.
candidates.structural_signature: A single output item fans out to multiple renderers whose products are presented together (concurrently or in immediate succession), each renderer targeting a different channel. The channels are redundant with respect to content: removing one loses a way of receiving the item but not the item itself.
candidates.pattern_curator_notes: The final set departs from consensus by moving rid 6271 above rid 17071 and rid 16653. The latter two are more novel, but their excerpts do not establish the pattern’s required redundancy: multimodal writing suggestions could differ by modality, and animation plus narration may divide spatial and verbal information. No score was adjusted by more than 0.3. Readers should distrust any implied outcome claims because the supplied excerpts describe mechanisms rather than measured effects. For rid 8046, the quote conclusively supports bilingual display but is less explicit about audible speech than the rater notes suggest; for rid 6271, games, images, and videos are complementary content and are not themselves evidence of this pattern—the qualifying mechanism is specifically the full voiceover of all text.

candidates.pattern_summary: One unit of system output is rendered in two or more sensory or representational channels at once — text plus speech, text plus image plus sound, or one language plus another.

The channels are redundant with respect to content: removing one loses a way of receiving the item but not the item itself.

For rid 8046, the quote conclusively supports bilingual display but is less explicit about audible speech than the rater notes suggest; for rid 6271, games, images, and videos are complementary content and are not themselves evidence of this pattern—the qualifying mechanism is specifically the full voiceover of all text.

candidates.title: GeoVisA11y: An AI-based Geovisualization Question-Answering System for Screen-Reader Users
candidates.why: GeoVisA11y preserves geographic topology as addressable state nodes and uses a persistent focus cursor with discrete cardinal commands, enabling screen-reader users to traverse the map rather than receive a flattened description.
candidates.over_the_runner_up: It is stronger than SeeChart because its direction-sensitive adjacency graph demonstrates genuinely structural navigation, whereas SeeChart only establishes linear movement between charts.
candidates.pattern_summary: A structured artifact is exposed as a traversable graph of positions that the user steps through with discrete commands, with the system's response delivered on a nonvisual channel.
candidates.structural_signature: The artifact is parsed into addressable nodes (items, points, layers, regions); the input surface is a small set of discrete move commands (next, previous, into, out of) plus queries; each move emits a nonvisual rendering of the node reached together with an orientation cue naming where in the structure that node sits. The load-bearing property is the *persistent cursor*: state is carried between commands so the same key means different things at different positions. Transplants to any structured content and any nonvisual channel — a directory tree read aloud, a menu stepped through by haptics.
candidates.pattern_curator_notes: I departed from the consensus by selecting rid 832 instead of the higher-scoring rid 5950. AskEase conflicts with the definition's explicit rejection of flattening into a single linear sequence, while ImageExplorer at least exposes hierarchical nodes and an into command. No individual score adjustment exceeds 0.3. All three selections have evidence limitations: GeoVisA11y does not explicitly quote the spoken response or orientation announcement; SeeChart's quote is truncated and establishes neither within-chart traversal nor an announced position; ImageExplorer is a borderline third exemplar because the supplied evidence emphasizes visible boundaries and does not establish a persistent cursor, nonvisual node rendering, or orientation cues. Only four of the stated seven candidates were supplied, so the selection is necessarily limited to those records.

candidates.title: AI at your Fingertips: Wearable Ring as a Low-Friction Interface for Agentic AI
candidates.why: The paper explicitly centers a screenless, “fire-and-forget” handoff, directly supporting the pattern’s complete nonvisual delegation and subsequent disengagement; however, the excerpt does not establish the full initiation–specification–termination sequence or prove that monitoring and mid-flight correction are impossible.
candidates.over_the_runner_up: It is the only supplied candidate, so there is no runner-up against which to make a comparative selection.
candidates.pattern_summary: The user hands a whole multi-step task to the system through a non-visual act and then stops attending to it; there is no display at any point in the loop.
candidates.structural_signature: The interaction consists of an initiation gesture, a specification uttered on a non-visual channel, and a terminating signal, with no display surface in the loop and no intermediate state exposed. Structurally this forbids monitoring, mid-flight correction, and selection among alternatives: the control flow has exactly one user decision point, at the start. Transplants to any delegation without a display — a button on a wearable, a voice command to an appliance.
candidates.pattern_curator_notes: Only one candidate was provided, so a defensible final set of three cannot be produced without inventing records; this output retains the sole eligible exemplar. I lowered its consensus score from 3.82 to 3.4 because the evidence establishes the subject matter unusually well but not the complete structural signature: the gesture, nonvisual specification channel, terminating signal, task complexity, absence of intermediate feedback, and impossibility of correction are all undocumented. Readers should therefore distrust any claim that the quoted excerpt alone demonstrates the entire interaction loop.

candidates.title: Exploring the impacts of semi-automated storytelling on programmers' comprehension of software histories
candidates.why: This is the most literal realization of the pattern: an existing non-prose list view is explicitly converted by GPT-4 into a narrative paragraph that serves as the readable output.
candidates.over_the_runner_up: It ranks above ViSTAR because the evidence identifies the source representation, conversion operation, and terminal prose surface more completely.
candidates.pattern_summary: Material that is not prose — extracted data, code, an algorithmic sequence, a probability, a structure — is converted into natural language and delivered in that form.
candidates.structural_signature: A non-prose source representation exists in the system, and a rendering step maps it to running natural language that is placed in the user-facing slot. The mapping is one-way and terminal: the prose is what the user consumes, and any downstream action is taken on the prose rather than on the source. The source may remain visible alongside, but the prose does not need to be re-parsed to be used.
candidates.pattern_curator_notes: I departed from the consensus by promoting rid 6267 from fourth to third and excluding rid 5807. RAVEN is highly consequential, but its quoted evidence shows a natural-language scene description without directly documenting the required source-to-prose mapping; EchoScriptor's evidence establishes that structure explicitly. The first two selections retain their consensus order. Readers should distrust strong claims about demonstrated impact: the evidence for rid 13939 is chiefly structural despite its comprehension framing, while the ViSTAR and EchoScriptor excerpts describe mechanisms but do not report measured outcome improvements. No score was adjusted by more than 0.3.

candidates.title: Keyframer: A Design Probe for Exploring LLM Assistance in 2D Animation Design
candidates.why: Keyframer cleanly separates an imperceptible generated representation from its display layer: completed LLM-generated CSS is combined with the fixed source SVG and rendered as an inline animation that users can directly judge. The evidence identifies the representation, rendering operation, fixed asset, and displayed result.
candidates.over_the_runner_up: Chosen over From Embeddings to Exploration because its ordinary CSS/SVG renderer is unambiguously separate from generation, whereas the latter relies on a learned decoder whose status as a content-neutral display layer is debatable.
candidates.pattern_summary: The model produces output in a representation the user cannot perceive directly — parameter streams, coordinate sequences, symbolic structures — and the system attaches a renderer that turns it into something viewable.
candidates.structural_signature: A rendering stage is inserted between generation and display: the generated representation R is mapped by a fixed, designer-chosen function into a perceptible form V, and only V appears in the interface. The mapping is deterministic and adds no content — everything shown is entailed by R plus fixed rendering assets. Where R is time-varying, V is commonly a sampled sequence laid out spatially. Transplants to sonifying a data stream, plotting a vector, animating a trajectory.
candidates.pattern_curator_notes: I departed from the consensus by excluding the second-ranked From Embeddings to Exploration and promoting Illuminating Memory from fourth. A learned latent decoder may synthesize details rather than function solely as the fixed, content-neutral renderer required by the structural signature; the RGB-to-light mapping is structurally cleaner and adds useful modality diversity. AgentHands was retained despite slight ambiguity about whether every event is model-generated because its parser-to-pose-to-animation separation is explicit. Readers should distrust claims about user impact: the supplied quotations establish implementation pipelines, not measured benefits. AgentHands is supported only by an abstract excerpt, and Illuminating Memory’s evidence does not describe the provenance or semantics of the RGB values beyond calling them model output.

candidates.title: Compendia: Automated Visual Storytelling Generation From Online Article Collection
candidates.why: The cluster glyph has an explicit, enumerable mapping: one radial bar encodes fact count and another encodes contributing-article count, making it the only candidate whose evidence directly establishes both named components and their geometric channels.
candidates.over_the_runner_up: Compendia outranks MetaGlyph because its quoted evidence reconstructs the glyph’s part-to-property mapping, whereas MetaGlyph only states that mappings and channels appear in a legend.
candidates.pattern_summary: Rather than reusing a standard chart type, the system introduces a new graphical mark whose geometry is designed around the specific property being communicated.
candidates.structural_signature: A composite graphical mark is defined by an explicit mapping from named components of the data property to named geometric channels of the mark (sector angle, chord endpoint, block extent, static shape standing for a time-varying quantity). The definition is enumerable — the paper can label the parts — and the mark is instantiated once per unit of data. Transplantable in the sense that any property with named components can be given such a mark; but note that what is shared across instances is the *act of designing* a mark, and the marks themselves have nothing structural in common beyond compositeness.
candidates.pattern_curator_notes: I departed from the consensus by promoting Compendia above MetaGlyph: structural completeness matters more here than MetaGlyph’s greater novelty and generalizability, and Compendia alone supplies an explicit named-property-to-named-part mapping in the quoted evidence. No score adjustment exceeds 0.3. Readers should distrust any implication that the MetaGlyph or FlowForge glyphs are reconstructable from the supplied excerpts: MetaGlyph’s quote refers to a legend without enumerating its mappings, and FlowForge names the encoded variables without assigning them to geometric channels. Compendia is the strongest evidenced fit, although its paired radial bars may be a relatively conventional composite rather than a radically new glyph form.
